title: ctlv: Prepare runtime introspection
overview: Adds drivers/ctlv/introspection.c, the handlers behind the CTLV root family's discovery queries: list the family chain, list a device's published operations with effective sizes and state, and describe the request/reply message schema of an operation. It is a leaf of the core layering: it consumes the device, schema and cursor/serialization layers from earlier patches and is only wired to a device by the dispatch patch; the Makefile change just adds it to the ctlv object so it is compile-checked.

files.purpose: Kbuild list of objects making up the ctlv module.

units.title: Add introspection.o to ctlv-y
units.summary: Links the new introspection object into ctlv.o so it is compiled when CONFIG_CTLV is enabled.
units.details: CONFIG_CTLV is not yet reachable from Kconfig in this patch, so this is a compile-check only.

files.purpose: Implements the three query callbacks of the root family (families dump, ops dump, op schema get). Each runs under the generic query machinery, builds its reply with the generated root-family serializers, and may be fragmented: when the reply buffer fills it returns ctlv_op_query_more() with a cursor and is re-invoked with that cursor via ctlv_op_query_cursor(ctx).

units.title: Header, includes and cursor packing
units.summary: Includes plus helpers that pack a (record, member) resume position into one u64 query cursor.
units.details: The low 48 bits hold the record index, the high 16 bits the member within the record, so a fragment can stop in the middle of a record.

units.title: ctlv_introspection_family_record()
units.summary: Writes one family-chain entry (id, name) into a nested entry, resuming at pos->member.
units.details: On a full buffer it returns false leaving pos->member at the first unwritten field; on success it resets member to 0.

units.title: ctlv_families_dump_query()
units.summary: Query callback that lists the families in the device's inheritance chain, root first.
units.details: Uses ctlv_family_ancestor() to walk from the root to the leaf; the chain is immutable so the generation is always 0 and a cursor stays valid.

units.title: Op snapshot helpers
units.summary: Takes a consistent copy of the dynamic-disable bitmap and state generation, and tests an op against it.
units.details: ctlv_introspection_snapshot_take() allocates the bitmap outside the lock and copies under transition_lock; ops with CTLV_OP_STATE_NONE are never disabled.

units.title: enum ctlv_introspection_op_field
units.summary: Ordered list of members of one op record; the order is the resume order.
units.details: Members double as pos->member values for fragmentation.

units.title: Op record field writers
units.summary: Maps each member index to the matching generated serializer, and decides which members apply to which op type.
units.details: Events carry only id, type and record length; actions add reply length; queries add reply min/suggested lengths. Sizes are the effective ones in op->sizes, including descendant fills.

units.title: ctlv_introspection_op_record()
units.summary: Writes one op entry, skipping inapplicable members and resuming from pos->member.
units.details: Returns false when the buffer is full, leaving the nest unfinished for the caller to abandon.

units.title: ctlv_ops_dump_query()
units.summary: Query callback listing the device's published operations with availability and disabled state.
units.details:
- Snapshot is taken once per fragment and freed via __free(bitmap).
- Walks ctlvdev->ops, which is frozen after init, so the record index is a stable cursor.
- The snapshot generation is reported so a client can detect state changes between fragments.

units.title: Schema walk state
units.summary: Structures for the schema description walk: a frame per nest level, the walk context, and a bounded list of leaf fields per node.
units.details: The cursor for schema queries is a count of leaves already emitted (ordinal), which allows a fragment boundary at any depth. Frames are heap allocated because they must outlive each open nest.

units.title: Field list helpers
units.summary: Append a typed (attr, kind, value) leaf to a node's field list, bounded by CTLV_INTROSPECTION_MAX_FIELDS.
units.details: ctlv_introspection_uint() is the common unsigned case.

units.title: ctlv_introspection_node_fields()
units.summary: Turns one schema node into the list of leaf attributes that describe it.
units.details: Always attr id, kind and max occurrences; then kind-specific bounds (range, flags mask, lengths, blob limits), an optional unit and scale, and a re-entry level count if the node recurses.

units.title: Nest opening and leaf writing
units.summary: Lazily open the nests down to a depth and write one leaf, skipping leaves already sent in earlier fragments.
units.details: ctlv_introspection_open() opens parents first, so an empty node produces no nest. ctlv_introspection_put() increments walk->ordinal only for successfully written (or skipped) leaves, so a failed write is the resume point.

units.title: ctlv_introspection_reenters()
units.summary: Resolves a recursive node to how many levels up its matching ancestor sits.
units.details: Matches an ancestor frame by tree and first_child; if none exists it sets walk->error to -EINVAL.

units.title: ctlv_introspection_children()
units.summary: Emits a node's declared children, then the members contributed by filled stubs.
units.details: Children are emitted as ATTRS (required) or OPTIONAL_ATTRS. For each stub schema on this node it looks up the fill via ctlv_schema_fill() for the device's family chain and recurses into the fill's members, forcing optionality when the stub placement is optional. Depth is bounded by CTLV_MAX_NEST_DEPTH.

units.title: ctlv_introspection_node()
units.summary: Describes one node: its fields, then its children, then closes its nest if it was opened.
units.details: A re-entering node reports its back-edge instead of repeating children, which is how unbounded nesting is described finitely.

units.title: ctlv_introspection_message()
units.summary: Describes the request or reply tree of an op as depth-0 frame.
units.details: Does nothing if the op has no such message (node_schemas is NULL).

units.title: ctlv_op_schema_get_query()
units.summary: Query callback that describes the request and reply schemas of one operation chosen by the request's op id.
units.details: Finds the op with ctlv_op_find() (published ops only, regardless of dynamic state), allocates the frame array, and walks request then reply. Fragmentation returns ctlv_op_query_more() with the leaf ordinal; generation is always 0 because schemas are immutable.
